correctness.rationale: The coefficient basis exhausts the 59048 nonzero cubic forms. Independent replay (python3 /workspace/checks/check3.py) computed rational zero and gradient tables and matched all 7488 qualifying coefficient codes to the frozen certificate, out of 35388 rationally nonsingular forms. It used the injective degree-three evaluation table on the 13 normalized projective points and all 11232 invertible matrices rather than generator closure; the three orbits exhausted the 3744 scalar classes, with sizes 936, 936, 1872 and stabilizers 6, 6, 3. Recomputed point counts 4, 7, 6, multiplicity profiles {1:12,4:1}, {1:2,2:9,4:2}, {1:6,2:3,3:4}, and external-line counts 2, 1, 1 all agree. Over the algebraic closure the first two gradients force Z=X=0, off the curves. For the third, Z=1 is necessary and the putative singularity has X=Y^2 and Y^3=Y+1, making the equation equal to Y^2, a contradiction. Thus the rational filter misses no smooth cases and none of the three orbits is geometrically singular. A line cannot fill, four smooth conic tangents with no triple concurrence cover only ten rational points, and a geometrically reducible irreducible conic has only its singular intersection as a rational point. These arguments establish the minimum degree and scope.
